title: Term 3 and 4 Examination
instructions: This paper covers the work of Terms 3 and 4.
This question paper consists of 5 questions. Answer ALL the questions.
Read each question carefully before you answer it.

sections.title: QUESTION 1: Short Stories
sections.instructions: Read the text below, then answer the questions.

context.title: The Red Bicycle (an original short story written for FreeSheet)
context.text:
Every afternoon Musa walked past Mr Botha's shop and stopped to look at the red bicycle in the window. It had a silver bell and a price tag of R1 800, which might as well have been a million.

Musa began washing cars at the taxi rank on Saturdays. His hands cracked in the winter cold, and twice older boys took his money. Still, the tin under his bed grew heavier. By September he had R1 650.

Then his little sister Zinhle fell ill. The clinic gave her medicine, but she needed proper shoes for the long walk to school, and his mother's purse was empty. Musa sat on his bed for a long time, the tin in his lap. In the morning he bought Zinhle a pair of black school shoes, and a small loaf of bread for the house.

In December, the red bicycle disappeared from the window. Musa did not look this time; he crossed the road instead. But on Christmas morning there was a knock at the door. Mr Botha stood there, holding the handlebars. 'Your mother told me about the shoes,' he said gruffly. 'A boy who works that hard should not walk everywhere. You can pay me the rest by sweeping my shop.'

Zinhle rang the silver bell all the way down the street.

questions.memo:
✓ Trait 1, e.g. hard-working (1) with evidence: washing cars in the cold every Saturday (½+½)
✓ Trait 2, e.g. selfless/caring: spends savings on his sister's shoes and bread (1)

sections.title: QUESTION 2: The Novel and Drama
sections.instructions: Read the text below, then answer the questions.

context.title: From the novel 'The Lighthouse Keeper's Granddaughter' (an original extract)
context.text:
Chapter 3

The storm arrived before supper, just as Grandpa Elias had said it would. Lerato pressed her nose to the cold window and watched the sea throw itself against the rocks like an angry dog on a chain.

"The lamp," Grandpa said suddenly, struggling to his feet. His knee had been stiff all week. "The lamp must be lit."

"Let me go," said Lerato. "I know how. I've watched you a hundred times."

He looked at her for a long moment. Three months ago, when her mother had sent her from Johannesburg to this lonely point of rock, she had refused even to climb the tower. Now she knew all one hundred and twelve steps by heart.

"The ships are counting on you," he said at last, and handed her the brass key.

The wind snatched at her jacket as she crossed the yard. Halfway up the stairs, the lights in the tower flickered and died. Lerato stood in the roaring dark, her heart hammering. Then she began to count the steps aloud.

questions.prompt: A smaller story that runs alongside the main story in a novel is called a:
Which figure of speech is used in 'the sea throw itself against the rocks like an angry dog on a chain'?
In the novel extract, Grandpa hands Lerato 'the brass key'. What does this action suggest about how he now sees her?
questions.memo:
✓ he trusts her / sees her as responsible or grown-up (1)
✓ evidence: he hesitates ('looked at her for a long moment') but then gives her the important task, saying 'The ships are counting on you' (1)

sections.title: QUESTION 3: Summary Writing
sections.instructions: Read the text below, then answer the questions.

context.title: Practice passage: Why Sleep Matters (original)
context.text: Many teenagers think sleep is a waste of time, but scientists disagree. While you sleep, your brain sorts and stores what you learned during the day, which is why a good night's sleep before a test can improve your marks more than staying up late to study. Sleep also allows your body to repair muscles and grow; in fact, most growth hormone is released during deep sleep. People who sleep well are less likely to catch colds, because sleep strengthens the immune system. A tired teenager is often grumpy, anxious or easily upset, since lack of sleep affects the part of the brain that controls emotions. Sleepy learners also struggle to concentrate in class. Finally, a regular bedtime can help you keep a healthy weight, as tiredness increases cravings for sugary snacks.

questions.prompt: Which of these should you leave OUT of a summary?
options: Key ideas in your own words

questions.prompt: In a summary you should copy the writer's sentences exactly.
Which word is a transition word that helps to link points in a summary paragraph?
List FOUR steps you would follow when writing a summary.
questions.memo: Any four (1 each): read instructions; skim the passage; underline points on the focus; leave out examples and repetition; rewrite in own words; link points; count words

questions.prompt: Decide whether each sentence from the passage is a main point or an example (detail).

pairs.left: People who sleep well are less likely to catch colds.
Sleep helps the brain store learning.

questions.prompt: Why must you state the number of words at the end of a summary?
questions.memo: ✓ To show that you have kept within the word limit (1)

questions.prompt: You may add your own opinion about the topic in a summary.
Rewrite in your own words, as one short point: 'lack of sleep affects the part of the brain that controls emotions'.
questions.memo: ✓✓ e.g. 'Tiredness makes it harder to manage feelings.' (own words, accurate, concise) (2)

sections.title: QUESTION 5: Diaries, Dialogues and Reviews
sections.instructions: Read the text below, then answer the questions.

context.title: Example diary entry (original)
context.text:
Friday, 7 June

Dear Diary

I can't believe it. I forgot my lines in the middle of the school play! The whole hall went silent and all I could hear was my heart thumping. Then Kagiso whispered the next line from behind the curtain and somehow I carried on.

Afterwards, Mom hugged me and said nobody even noticed. I'm not sure that's true, but I feel a bit better. Tomorrow I'm going to thank Kagiso properly. Maybe I'll even try out for next year's play.

context.title: Example dialogue (original)
context.text:
[Context: Neo and his older sister Palesa are in the kitchen. Neo wants to borrow her laptop.]

NEO: (smiling sweetly) Palesa, you know you're my favourite sister?
PALESA: I'm your only sister. What do you want?
NEO: Just your laptop. For an hour. It's for a school project, I promise.
PALESA: (folding her arms) Last time it was 'for a school project', I found a game on my desktop.
NEO: That was research!
PALESA: (laughing) Fine. One hour. And you wash the dishes tonight.
NEO: Deal! (grabs the laptop and runs off)
